record.paper_title: Computational issues for linear periodic systems: paradigms, algorithms, open problems
record.context_brief: Periodic descriptor realization from lifted systems
record.original_question: For arbitrary lifted systems arising from discrete-time periodic models, can one compute a corresponding periodic descriptor-system realization, including cases in which the lifted-system computations yield a non-causal system? In particular, is there a general algorithm that reconstructs a periodic descriptor realization from such arbitrary lifted representations without losing the relevant structure?

evidence.quote: For example, if the result is a non-causal system, then apparently there exists even no algorithm to compute the corresponding periodic descriptor system realisation.
For discrete-time systems, we mention the lack of algorithms for computing ... periodic descriptor system realisation of arbitrary lifted systems

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a discrete-time linear periodic descriptor system of period $N\ge 1$ of the form
$$E_k x_{k+1} = A_k x_k + B_k u_k,\qquad y_k = C_k x_k + D_k u_k,\qquad k\in\mathbb{Z},$$
where $E_k,A_k\in\mathbb{R}^{n_{k+1}\times n_k}$, $B_k\in\mathbb{R}^{n_{k+1}\times m}$, $C_k\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times n_k}$, $D_k\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times m}$, with all matrices $N$-periodic in $k$. Associated with such a system is its lifted (time-invariant) representation, obtained by stacking $N$ consecutive inputs and outputs and eliminating intermediate states, producing an LTI input/output operator (which may be improper, i.e. correspond to a non-causal lifted system).

Problem. Given an arbitrary lifted LTI realization $(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{B},\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D})$ — including the case in which the corresponding transfer matrix is improper, so that the lifted system is non-causal — design a general algorithm that constructs a periodic descriptor realization $\{(E_k,A_k,B_k,C_k,D_k)\}_{k=0}^{N-1}$ whose lifting equals (or is equivalent to) the given lifted system, preserving the periodic and descriptor structure. Equivalently, exhibit a constructive procedure that inverts the lifting map for arbitrary, possibly non-causal, lifted systems and yields a corresponding periodic descriptor realization.
artifact.status_search_result: Related work exists on minimal periodic realizations, anti-causal/non-causal realizations of inverse periodic systems via outer-inner factorization, and structure-preserving reductions of lifted system pencils. However, no source clearly establishes a general algorithm that, from an arbitrary (possibly non-causal) lifted representation, constructs a corresponding periodic descriptor realization in the discrete-time case. The status therefore remains unclear from available evidence.

status_evidence.title: On computing minimal realizations of periodic descriptor systems (A. Varga)
status_evidence.snippet: Addresses minimal realization of periodic descriptor systems but does not give a general procedure to recover a periodic descriptor realization from arbitrary, possibly non-causal lifted systems.
status_evidence.claim: Existing minimal-realization algorithms target causal/regular settings; the non-causal lifted case is not fully covered.

status_evidence.title: Decomposition and Noncausal Realization of Unstable LPTV System
status_evidence.snippet: Develops anti-causal/noncausal realizations for unstable LPTV systems via factorization techniques.
status_evidence.claim: Partial techniques exist for non-causal periodic realizations but not a general inverse-lifting algorithm for arbitrary lifted systems.

status_evidence.title: Computing Minimal Discrete Time-Varying Forward/Backward Periodic Realizations of Rational Matrices
status_evidence.snippet: Considers forward/backward periodic realizations of rational matrices.
status_evidence.claim: Demonstrates ongoing work on the realization problem in periodic settings, without a complete general solution for arbitrary lifted descriptor cases.
